            <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"NewsArticle","headline":"Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy?","articleBody":"Not too long ago, if you wanted AirPods with active noise cancellation, you had one option: the AirPods Pro. For several years following, Apple kept ANC strictly limited to its premium options: the Pros and the AirPods Max. Then in 2024, Apple threw a curveball AirPods 4, offering two models, with the more expensive one featuring ANC on a sub-$200 pair of AirPods for the first time ever.And with the announcement of the AirPods 5 at the brand's "Surprise and Shine" keynote event on Sept. 9, AirPods without ANC have become a thing of the past altogether. At $129 and $149, both the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case come with ANC (not to mention live translation). It also means there are now three options for noise-canceling earbuds from Apple.

        SEE ALSO:
        
            The 11 best wireless earbuds we've ever tested
            
        
    
In deciding what to get, it's worth weighing out what you need out of your earbuds. To help you make your choice, we broke down the differences between the AirPods 5 (with and without the Wireless Charging Case) and the AirPods Pro 3, Apple's premium wireless earbuds. We just started testing the new AirPods, so stay tuned for a true head-to-head comparison. In the meantime, this is how they compare in specs, features, and form factor.First: the AirPods 4 vs. the AirPods 5Before we jump into the full comparison, a quick note on why we're not breaking down AirPods 4 vs. 5 comparison — it's because there really is none. The $129 AirPods 4 feature no noise cancellation, while the ones that do go for $179. Sure, you can catch them on sale for $99 a lot of the time, but you also won't be able to take advantage of the improved ANC, sound quality, Live Translation, and improved controls of the AirPods 5. So, unless you're trying to spend more money on an inferior product, I'd recommend sticking with the newer AirPods. (That said, the difference isn't so stark that AirPods 4 users need to upgrade). Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Price and specsPricing AirPods 5 — $129AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — $149AirPods Pro 3 — $249SpecsAirPods 5Battery: Four hours of listening time (six without ANC), 20 hours total with caseListening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback and callsCharging: USB-C charging caseFind My: Not available on this charging caseAirPods 5 with Wireless Charging CaseBattery: Five hours of listening time (seven without ANC), 22 hours total with case Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controlsCharging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatibleFind My: Speaker included to work with Find MyAirPods Pro 3Battery: Eight hours of listening time (10 with Transparency mode and Hearing Aid feature) Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controlsCharging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatibleFind My: Speaker included to work with Find MyApple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Design
    
                    


            
            
            The AirPods Pro 3 have interchangeable foam-infused silicon ear tips, opposed to the open ear design of the AirPods 5.
            Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable
        
    
Most notably, the two earbuds will wear differently. The AirPods Pro 3 feature silicone ear tips for a true in-ear design, while the AirPods 5 stick to the open-ear design. (It should be noted that, though these are technically open earbuds, they sit somewhat in the ear canal, unlike other clip or hook style open earbuds.) Without ear tips to create a tight seal, noise cancellation will take a hit with the AirPods 5.
        SEE ALSO:
        
            The 7 best open earbuds stay put, sound great, and keep us aware of the world
            
        
    
If you opt for the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, the earbuds' stems feature swipe volume controls, just like the AirPods Pro. Both AirPods 5 have playback and call controls on the stems.As for the charging case, the Pro and standard AirPods stick to the usual deviation, with the Pros featuring a shorter, wider look. Both the Pros and the more expensive AirPods 5 will have wireless charging and Find My capabilities, but the Pros get the slightest edge with a lanyard loop.The Pro 3 and both AirPods 5, however, have a water- and dust-resistance rating of IP57.Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Sound quality
    
                    


            
            
            A multichannel acoustic architecture comes to the AirPods 5.
            Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable
        
    
Again, Mashable's team hasn't yet had the chance to finish testing the new AirPods. We can say that, per Apple, the multiport acoustic architecture in the AirPods 5 was inspired by AirPods Pro 3 design. Considering the discrepancy in price, however, and the AirPods Pro 3 in-ear design, it's safe to say the Pros will have the superior sound quality.Previously, AirPods haven't offered a manually adjustable equalizer, but that's set to change with iOS 27. If you have an iPhone that supports iOS 27, you'll soon be able to access custom EQ settings for your AirPods.Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Noise cancellationAccording to Apple, the AirPods Pro 3 have up to three times more noise cancellation than the AirPods 5. While ANC is difficult to quantify, it does make sense that the in-ear design and the foam-infused silicone ear tips of the Pros would offer, at the very least, more passive noise cancellation. That said, the AirPods 5 ANC isn't anything to scoff at. Apple claims the ANC on the new generation is one and a half times more powerful than the ANC found on the AirPods 4 with ANC. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Battery lifeThis is pretty much as it's written on the tin — the AirPods Pro 3 undeniably have the superior battery life, bringing eight hours per charge with ANC (and 24 hours in the case). The $149 AirPods 5 come next, with five hours per charge with ANC (and 22 hours in the case). The AirPods 5 remain at the same level as the AirPods 4 with ANC, at four hours per charge with ANC (and 20 hours in the case). While the AirPods Pro 3 do have double the per-charge battery life of the standard AirPods 5, it's worth remembering that the Pro 3 are also $120 more — nearly the price of another pair of AirPods 5.  Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Extra features
    
                    


            
            
            The Pro 3 are great companions for a workout.
            Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable
        
    
The Pros are designed to offer an all-encompassing experience, and their extra features show exactly that. The Pros have a built-in heart rate monitor that works with the Apple Fitness app and other compatible health apps, making them especially great for exercise. The Pro 3 also have a hearing test, aid, and hearing protection features.Both the AirPods 5 and the Pro 3 have Live Translation capabilities. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which is better? If you're wearing earbuds daily, for multiple hours of the day, the longer battery life, versatility, and superior ANC and sound quality of the AirPods Pro 3 are likely worth the investment. However, for more casual users, the AirPods 5 allow for an experience of some of the better parts of Apple's noise-cancelling experience without the hefty price tag to match.

                    <p>Not too long ago, if you wanted AirPods with active noise cancellation, you had one option: the AirPods Pro. For several years following, Apple kept ANC strictly limited to its premium options: the Pros and the AirPods Max. Then in 2024, Apple threw a curveball <a href="https://mashable.com/article/airpods-4-hands-on-review" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">AirPods 4,</a> offering two models, with the more expensive one featuring ANC on a sub-$200 pair of AirPods for the first time ever.</p><p>And with the announcement of the <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-airpods-5-announcement-iphone-event-2026-clone" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">AirPods 5</a> at the brand's "<a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-event-2026-live-updates-iphone-18-announcements" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">Surprise and Shine" keynote event on Sept. 9</a>, AirPods without ANC have become a thing of the past altogether. At $129 and $149, both the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case come with ANC (not to mention live translation). It also means there are now three options for <a href="https://mashable.com/roundup/best-noise-cancelling-earbuds-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">noise-canceling earbuds</a> from Apple.</p><div class="lg:grid lg:grid-cols-2 lg:gap-4 lg:mx-auto lg:max-w-3xl">

<h2 id="first-the-airpods-4-vs-the-airpods-5">First: the AirPods 4 vs. the AirPods 5</h2><p>Before we jump into the full comparison, a quick note on why we're not breaking down AirPods 4 vs. 5 comparison — it's because there really is none. The $129 AirPods 4 feature no noise cancellation, while the ones that do go for $179. Sure, you can <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/sept-10-airpods-4-deal" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">catch them on sale for $99</a> a lot of the time, but you also won't be able to take advantage of the improved ANC, sound quality, Live Translation, and improved controls of the AirPods 5. </p><p>So, unless you're trying to spend more money on an inferior product, I'd recommend sticking with the newer AirPods. (That said, the difference isn't so stark that AirPods 4 users <em>need </em>to upgrade). </p><h2 id="apple-airpods-5-vs-airpods-pro-3-price-and-specs">Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Price and specs</h2><h3>Pricing </h3><ul><li><p>AirPods 5 — <strong>$129</strong></p></li><li><p>AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — <strong>$149</strong></p></li><li><p>AirPods Pro 3 — <strong>$249</strong></p></li></ul><h3>Specs</h3><p><strong>AirPods 5</strong></p><ul><li><p>Battery: Four hours of listening time (six without ANC), 20 hours total with case</p></li><li><p>Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency</p></li><li><p>Controls: Force sensor for playback and calls</p></li><li><p>Charging: USB-C charging case</p></li><li><p>Find My: Not available on this charging case</p></li></ul><p><strong>AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case</strong></p><ul><li><p>Battery: Five hours of listening time (seven without ANC), 22 hours total with case </p></li><li><p>Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency</p></li><li><p>Controls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controls</p></li><li><p>Charging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatible</p></li><li><p>Find My: Speaker included to work with Find My</p></li></ul><p><strong>AirPods Pro 3</strong></p><ul><li><p>Battery: Eight hours of listening time (10 with Transparency mode and Hearing Aid feature) </p></li><li><p>Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency</p></li><li><p>Controls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controls</p></li><li><p>Charging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatible</p></li><li><p>Find My: Speaker included to work with Find My</p></li></ul><h2 id="apple-airpods-5-vs-airpods-pro-3-design">Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Design</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">

<p>If you opt for the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, the earbuds' stems feature swipe volume controls, just like the AirPods Pro. Both AirPods 5 have playback and call controls on the stems.</p><p>As for the charging case, the Pro and standard AirPods stick to the usual deviation, with the Pros featuring a shorter, wider look. Both the Pros and the more expensive AirPods 5 will have wireless charging and Find My capabilities, but the Pros get the slightest edge with a lanyard loop.</p><p>The Pro 3 and both AirPods 5, however, have a water- and dust-resistance rating of IP57.</p><h2 id="apple-airpods-5-vs-airpods-pro-3-sound-quality">Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Sound quality</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">

Considering the discrepancy in price, however, and the AirPods Pro 3 in-ear design, it's safe to say the Pros will have the superior sound quality.</p><p>Previously, AirPods haven't offered a manually adjustable equalizer, but <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-ios-27-best-features" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">that's set to change with iOS 27</a>. Apple claims the ANC on the new generation is one and a half times more powerful than the ANC found on the AirPods 4 with ANC. </p><h2 id="apple-airpods-5-vs-airpods-pro-3-battery-life">Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Battery life</h2><p>This is pretty much as it's written on the tin — the AirPods Pro 3 undeniably have the superior battery life, bringing eight hours per charge with ANC (and 24 hours in the case). The $149 AirPods 5 come next, with five hours per charge with ANC (and 22 hours in the case). The AirPods 5 remain at the same level as the AirPods 4 with ANC, at four hours per charge with ANC (and 20 hours in the case). </p><p>While the AirPods Pro 3 do have double the per-charge battery life of the standard AirPods 5, it's worth remembering that the Pro 3 are also $120 more — nearly the price of another pair of AirPods 5.  </p><h2 id="apple-airpods-5-vs-airpods-pro-3-extra-features">Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Extra features</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">

Do you really need to splurge on the AirPods Pro 3?  By  Bethany Allard Bethany Allard Lead Shopping Reporter Bethany Allard is a Los Angeles-based shopping reporter at Mashable covering beauty tech, dating, sex and relationships, and headphones. That basically means she puts her hair through a lot, scrolls through a lot of dating apps, and rotates through a lot of different headphones. In addition to testing out and rounding up the best products, she also covers deals for Mashable, paying an especially obsessive amount of attention to Apple deals and prices. That knowledge comes in handy when she's covering shopping holidays like Prime Day and Black Friday, which she's now done for three years at Mashable. Not too long ago, if you wanted AirPods with active noise cancellation, you had one option: the AirPods Pro. For several years following, Apple kept ANC strictly limited to its premium options: the Pros and the AirPods Max. Then in 2024, Apple threw a curveball AirPods 4, offering two models, with the more expensive one featuring ANC on a sub-$200 pair of AirPods for the first time ever. And with the announcement of the AirPods 5 at the brand's " Surprise and Shine" keynote event on Sept. 9 , AirPods without ANC have become a thing of the past altogether. At $129 and $149, both the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case come with ANC (not to mention live translation). It also means there are now three options for  noise-canceling earbuds  from Apple. Apple AirPods 5 earbuds $129 at Amazon   Pre-order Here at Amazon Pre-order Here at Apple.com Pre-order Here at Walmart Apple AirPods Pro 3 Noise Cancelling Heart Rate Wireless Earbuds $199 at Amazon $249 Save $50   See It at Amazon See It at Walmart SEE ALSO: The 11 best wireless earbuds we've ever tested In deciding what to get, it's worth weighing out what you need out of your earbuds. To help you make your choice, we broke down the differences between the AirPods 5 (with and without the Wireless Charging Case) and the AirPods Pro 3 , Apple's premium wireless earbuds. We just started testing the new AirPods, so stay tuned for a true head-to-head comparison. In the meantime, this is how they compare in specs, features, and form factor. You May Also Like First: the AirPods 4 vs. the AirPods 5 Before we jump into the full comparison, a quick note on why we're not breaking down AirPods 4 vs. 5 comparison — it's because there really is none. The $129 AirPods 4 feature no noise cancellation, while the ones that do go for $179. Sure, you can catch them on sale for $99 a lot of the time, but you also won't be able to take advantage of the improved ANC, sound quality, Live Translation, and improved controls of the AirPods 5. So, unless you're trying to spend more money on an inferior product, I'd recommend sticking with the newer AirPods. (That said, the difference isn't so stark that AirPods 4 users need to upgrade). Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Price and specs Pricing AirPods 5 — $129 AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — $149 AirPods Pro 3 — $249 Specs AirPods 5 Battery: Four hours of listening time (six without ANC), 20 hours total with case Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency Controls: Force sensor for playback and calls Charging: USB-C charging case Find My: Not available on this charging case AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case Battery: Five hours of listening time (seven without ANC), 22 hours total with case Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency Controls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controls Charging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatible Find My: Speaker included to work with Find My AirPods Pro 3 Battery: Eight hours of listening time (10 with Transparency mode and Hearing Aid feature) Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparency Controls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controls Charging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatible Find My: Speaker included to work with Find My Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Design The AirPods Pro 3 have interchangeable foam-infused silicon ear tips, opposed to the open ear design of the AirPods 5. Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable Most notably, the two earbuds will wear differently. The AirPods Pro 3 feature silicone ear tips for a true in-ear design, while the AirPods 5 stick to the open-ear design. (It should be noted that, though these are technically  open earbuds , they sit somewhat in the ear canal, unlike other clip or hook style open earbuds.) Without ear tips to create a tight seal, noise cancellation will take a hit with the AirPods 5. Mashable Light Speed Want more out-of-this world tech, space and science stories? SEE ALSO: The 7 best open earbuds stay put, sound great, and keep us aware of the world If you opt for the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, the earbuds' stems feature swipe volume controls, just like the AirPods Pro. Both AirPods 5 have playback and call controls on the stems. As for the charging case, the Pro and standard AirPods stick to the usual deviation, with the Pros featuring a shorter, wider look. Both the Pros and the more expensive AirPods 5 will have wireless charging and Find My capabilities, but the Pros get the slightest edge with a lanyard loop. The Pro 3 and both AirPods 5, however, have a water- and dust-resistance rating of IP57. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Sound quality A multichannel acoustic architecture comes to the AirPods 5. Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable Again, Mashable's team hasn't yet had the chance to finish testing the new AirPods. We can say that, per Apple, the multiport acoustic architecture in the AirPods 5 was inspired by AirPods Pro 3 design. Considering the discrepancy in price, however, and the AirPods Pro 3 in-ear design, it's safe to say the Pros will have the superior sound quality. Previously, AirPods haven't offered a manually adjustable equalizer, but that's set to change with iOS 27 . If you have an iPhone that supports iOS 27 , you'll soon be able to access custom EQ settings for your AirPods. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Noise cancellation According to Apple, the AirPods Pro 3 have up to three times more noise cancellation than the AirPods 5. While ANC is difficult to quantify, it does make sense that the in-ear design and the foam-infused silicone ear tips of the Pros would offer, at the very least, more passive noise cancellation. That said, the AirPods 5 ANC isn't anything to scoff at. Apple claims the ANC on the new generation is one and a half times more powerful than the ANC found on the AirPods 4 with ANC. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Battery life This is pretty much as it's written on the tin — the AirPods Pro 3 undeniably have the superior battery life, bringing eight hours per charge with ANC (and 24 hours in the case). The $149 AirPods 5 come next, with five hours per charge with ANC (and 22 hours in the case). The AirPods 5 remain at the same level as the AirPods 4 with ANC, at four hours per charge with ANC (and 20 hours in the case). While the AirPods Pro 3 do have double the per-charge battery life of the standard AirPods 5, it's worth remembering that the Pro 3 are also $120 more — nearly the price of another pair of AirPods 5. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Extra features The Pro 3 are great companions for a workout. Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable The Pros are designed to offer an all-encompassing experience, and their extra features show exactly that. The Pros have a built-in heart rate monitor that works with the Apple Fitness app and other compatible health apps, making them especially great for exercise . The Pro 3 also have a hearing test, aid, and hearing protection features. Both the AirPods 5 and the Pro 3 have Live Translation capabilities. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which is better? If you're wearing earbuds daily, for multiple hours of the day, the longer battery life, versatility, and superior ANC and sound quality of the AirPods Pro 3 are likely worth the investment. However, for more casual users, the AirPods 5 allow for an experience of some of the better parts of Apple's noise-cancelling experience without the hefty price tag to match. jsonld_parsed.headline: Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy?
jsonld_parsed.articleBody:
Not too long ago, if you wanted AirPods with active noise cancellation, you had one option: the AirPods Pro. For several years following, Apple kept ANC strictly limited to its premium options: the Pros and the AirPods Max. Then in 2024, Apple threw a curveball AirPods 4, offering two models, with the more expensive one featuring ANC on a sub-$200 pair of AirPods for the first time ever.And with the announcement of the AirPods 5 at the brand's "Surprise and Shine" keynote event on Sept. 9, AirPods without ANC have become a thing of the past altogether. At $129 and $149, both the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case come with ANC (not to mention live translation). It also means there are now three options for noise-canceling earbuds from Apple.
            
    
    
                                                        
    
                                        
    
        
                                        
                                            
    Apple AirPods 5 earbuds
                                    
                                        
                    
                                                    $129
                                                             at Amazon
                                                        
                                                                    
                
                                         
                    
        
                                                                            
    Pre-order Here at Amazon
                                                        
    Pre-order Here at Apple.com
                                                        
    Pre-order Here at Walmart
                                            
    

            
    
    
                                                        
    
                                        
    
        
                                        
                                            
    Apple AirPods Pro 3 Noise Cancelling Heart Rate Wireless Earbuds
                                    
                                        
                    
                                                    $199
                                                             at Amazon
                                                        
                                                                                                            $249
                                                                                         Save $50
                                                                        
                
                                         
                    
        
                                                                            
    See It at Amazon
                                                        
    See It at Walmart
                                            
    

    

        SEE ALSO:
        
            The 11 best wireless earbuds we've ever tested
            
        
    
In deciding what to get, it's worth weighing out what you need out of your earbuds. To help you make your choice, we broke down the differences between the AirPods 5 (with and without the Wireless Charging Case) and the AirPods Pro 3, Apple's premium wireless earbuds. We just started testing the new AirPods, so stay tuned for a true head-to-head comparison. In the meantime, this is how they compare in specs, features, and form factor.First: the AirPods 4 vs. the AirPods 5Before we jump into the full comparison, a quick note on why we're not breaking down AirPods 4 vs. 5 comparison — it's because there really is none. The $129 AirPods 4 feature no noise cancellation, while the ones that do go for $179. Sure, you can catch them on sale for $99 a lot of the time, but you also won't be able to take advantage of the improved ANC, sound quality, Live Translation, and improved controls of the AirPods 5. So, unless you're trying to spend more money on an inferior product, I'd recommend sticking with the newer AirPods. (That said, the difference isn't so stark that AirPods 4 users need to upgrade). Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Price and specsPricing AirPods 5 — $129AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — $149AirPods Pro 3 — $249SpecsAirPods 5Battery: Four hours of listening time (six without ANC), 20 hours total with caseListening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback and callsCharging: USB-C charging caseFind My: Not available on this charging caseAirPods 5 with Wireless Charging CaseBattery: Five hours of listening time (seven without ANC), 22 hours total with case Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controlsCharging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatibleFind My: Speaker included to work with Find MyAirPods Pro 3Battery: Eight hours of listening time (10 with Transparency mode and Hearing Aid feature) Listening modes: Adaptive audio and transparencyControls: Force sensor for playback, calls, and volume swipe controlsCharging: USB-C charging case, MagSafe, Qi compatibleFind My: Speaker included to work with Find MyApple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Design
    
                    


            
            
            The AirPods Pro 3 have interchangeable foam-infused silicon ear tips, opposed to the open ear design of the AirPods 5.
            Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable
        
    
Most notably, the two earbuds will wear differently. The AirPods Pro 3 feature silicone ear tips for a true in-ear design, while the AirPods 5 stick to the open-ear design. (It should be noted that, though these are technically open earbuds, they sit somewhat in the ear canal, unlike other clip or hook style open earbuds.) Without ear tips to create a tight seal, noise cancellation will take a hit with the AirPods 5.
        SEE ALSO:
        
            The 7 best open earbuds stay put, sound great, and keep us aware of the world
            
        
    
If you opt for the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, the earbuds' stems feature swipe volume controls, just like the AirPods Pro. Both AirPods 5 have playback and call controls on the stems.As for the charging case, the Pro and standard AirPods stick to the usual deviation, with the Pros featuring a shorter, wider look. Both the Pros and the more expensive AirPods 5 will have wireless charging and Find My capabilities, but the Pros get the slightest edge with a lanyard loop.The Pro 3 and both AirPods 5, however, have a water- and dust-resistance rating of IP57.Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Sound quality
    
                    


            
            
            A multichannel acoustic architecture comes to the AirPods 5.
            Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable
        
    
Again, Mashable's team hasn't yet had the chance to finish testing the new AirPods. We can say that, per Apple, the multiport acoustic architecture in the AirPods 5 was inspired by AirPods Pro 3 design. Considering the discrepancy in price, however, and the AirPods Pro 3 in-ear design, it's safe to say the Pros will have the superior sound quality.Previously, AirPods haven't offered a manually adjustable equalizer, but that's set to change with iOS 27. If you have an iPhone that supports iOS 27, you'll soon be able to access custom EQ settings for your AirPods.Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Noise cancellationAccording to Apple, the AirPods Pro 3 have up to three times more noise cancellation than the AirPods 5. While ANC is difficult to quantify, it does make sense that the in-ear design and the foam-infused silicone ear tips of the Pros would offer, at the very least, more passive noise cancellation. That said, the AirPods 5 ANC isn't anything to scoff at. Apple claims the ANC on the new generation is one and a half times more powerful than the ANC found on the AirPods 4 with ANC. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Battery lifeThis is pretty much as it's written on the tin — the AirPods Pro 3 undeniably have the superior battery life, bringing eight hours per charge with ANC (and 24 hours in the case). The $149 AirPods 5 come next, with five hours per charge with ANC (and 22 hours in the case). The AirPods 5 remain at the same level as the AirPods 4 with ANC, at four hours per charge with ANC (and 20 hours in the case). While the AirPods Pro 3 do have double the per-charge battery life of the standard AirPods 5, it's worth remembering that the Pro 3 are also $120 more — nearly the price of another pair of AirPods 5.  Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Extra features
    
                    


            
            
            The Pro 3 are great companions for a workout.
            Credit: Adam Doud / Mashable
        
    
The Pros are designed to offer an all-encompassing experience, and their extra features show exactly that. The Pros have a built-in heart rate monitor that works with the Apple Fitness app and other compatible health apps, making them especially great for exercise. The Pro 3 also have a hearing test, aid, and hearing protection features.Both the AirPods 5 and the Pro 3 have Live Translation capabilities. Apple AirPods 5 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which is better? If you're wearing earbuds daily, for multiple hours of the day, the longer battery life, versatility, and superior ANC and sound quality of the AirPods Pro 3 are likely worth the investment. However, for more casual users, the AirPods 5 allow for an experience of some of the better parts of Apple's noise-cancelling experience without the hefty price tag to match.

So in this PS5 vs. PS5 Slim face off, I'll be helping you decide which console is best for you.With the recent launch of the upgraded PS5 Pro console, now might be the perfect opportunity to snag a slightly older — yet still incredibly powerful — PS5.With potential sweet deals, or even permanent price drops on the horizon, it’s essential to know exactly what you’re getting (and not getting) with the PS5 and PS5 Slim.\n        SEE ALSO:\n        \n            The price of Sony's PS5 Pro is 'brutal' and the internet hates it\n            \n        \n    \nPS5 vs. PS5 Slim: priceFor context, the original, non-slim PS5 has two versions: a digital one (without a disc drive) and one with a disc drive. The same can be said for the PS5 Slim; it's got a digital version and a disc one. For whatever reason, Sony decided to not drop the prices of the new PS5 Slim models. The PS5 Slim with a disc drive is still $499, while the PS5 Slim without a disc drive is $449 — or a $50 increase over the original PS5 digital-only console.PS5 Slim (no disc drive) - $449PS5 Slim         \n    \n        \n                                        \n                                            \n    PS5 Slim (no disc drive)\n                                    \n                                        \n                    \n                                                    $494.40\n                                                             at Amazon\n                                                        \n                                                                    \n                \n                                         \n                    \n        \n                                                                            \n    Shop Now at Amazon\n                                                        \n    Shop Now at PlayStation Store\n                                            \n    \n\n\n    \n    \n                                                        \n    \n                                        \n    \n        \n                                        \n                                            \n    Sony PlayStation 5\n                                    \n                                        \n                    \n                                                    $704.99\n                                                             at Walmart\n                                                        \n                                                                    \n                \n                                         \n                    \n        \n                                                                            \n    Get Deal at Walmart\n                                                        \n    Get Deal at Amazon\n                                                        \n    Get Deal at Amazon\n                                            \n    \n\nWith that in mind, yes, the digital-only PS5 Slim is a money-saver in comparison to the one with a disc drive, but not in comparison to the digital-only model that launched in 2020. The new price also means that buying a digital model before purchasing the additional disc drive would cost more than just snagging the version with a built-in drive. I don't really have a good explanation for that.My only advice is this: If you want a PS5 that only costs $399, you better get one now. This is an important note: Once the existing stock of both original models sells out, the new slim models will replace them on store shelves. PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: sizeObviously, size is what many gamers are most concerned about here, so let's get right to it. Looking at Sony's stated dimensions, you can see that the new PS5 is indeed smaller than the original:Original PS5 (disc version): 104mm (height) x 390mm (width) x 260mm (depth)PS5 Slim (disc version): 96mm (height) x 358mm (width) x 216mm (depth)Original PS5 (digital version): 92mm x 390mm x 260mmPS5 Slim (digital version): 80mm x 358mm x 216mm\n    \n                    \n\n\n            \n            \n            \n            Credit: Sony\n        \n    \nIn other words, per Sony's announcement blog post, that's about a 30 percent reduction in total volume. That's definitely an improvement, but there's some important context missing in just those raw numbers. The Verge ran a digital size comparison and discovered that both new models are still substantially larger than the Xbox Series X. In other words, this \"slim\" console is still pretty dang big.For a visual comparison, check out this awesome PS5 Slim vs. Regular Reddit post.PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: performance and storageAnother important aspect of the new PS5 models to get out of the way is that they have the exact same internal capabilities as the originals. This isn't a PS4 vs. PS4 Pro situation. Games will run exactly the same across the spectrum of PS5 consoles.\n    \n                    \n\n\n            \n            \n            \n            Credit: Sony\n        \n    \nOne little internal bonus that owners of the new PS5s get, however, comes in the form of expanded storage. For some reason, the original PS5 only had 825GB of onboard storage, with the option to expand via external SSDs. The new ones have a full 1TB of built-in space, so you can install a few extra games depending on how big they are.PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: disc driveJust like at the PS5's launch in late 2020, there are two PS5 Slim models. One of them has a built-in disc drive and the other one is digital-only.\n    \n                    \n\n\n            \n            \n            \n            Credit: Sony\n        \n    \nWell, sort of, anyway. There's an optional detachable disc drive you can buy for $79.99. It's a little goofy looking, but it should do exactly what you think it does. For physical media collectors, the disc drive is a must-buy.It's worth noting, however, that the PS5 Slim, unlike the OG PS5, does not come with a vertical stand in the box. That's definitely an improvement, but there's some important context missing in just those raw numbers. <a href="https://www.theverge.com/2023/10/10/23911388/new-ps5-model-slim-size-comparison" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body" title="(opens in a new window)"><em>The Verge</em></a> ran a digital size comparison and discovered that both new models are still substantially larger than the Xbox Series X. </p><p>In other words, this "slim" console is still pretty dang big.</p><p><em>For a visual comparison, check out this awesome <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/playstation/comments/174s1s8/ps5_vs_ps5_slim_size_comparison/" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body" title="(opens in a new window)">PS5 Slim vs. Regular</a></em><em> Reddit post.</em></p><div class="related-stories" data-ga-impression data-ga-module="related_stories" data-ga-element="related_stories_link" data-ga-item="title">

<h2 id="ps5-vs-ps5-slim-performance-and-storage">PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: performance and storage</h2><p>Another important aspect of the new PS5 models to get out of the way is that they have the exact same internal capabilities as the originals. This isn't a PS4 vs. PS4 Pro situation. Games will run exactly the same across the spectrum of PS5 consoles.</p><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">
    <div class="flex justify-center">
                    <img class="w-full" src="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-3.fill.size_2000x1334.v1697141760.jpg" alt="PS5 Slim" width="2000" height="1334" loading="lazy" srcset="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-3.fill.size_800x534.v1697141760.jpg 800w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-3.fill.size_1400x934.v1697141760.jpg 1400w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-3.fill.size_2000x1334.v1697141760.jpg 2000w" sizes="(max-width: 1408px) 100vw, 1408px">


            </div>
            <div class="mt-2 subtitle-2 font-sans ">
            <span class="normal-case text-gray-1000"></span>
            <span class="text-gray-600 credit">Credit: Sony</span>
        </div>
    </div>
<p>One little internal bonus that owners of the new PS5s get, however, comes in the form of expanded storage. For some reason, the original PS5 only had 825GB of onboard storage, with the option to expand via external SSDs. The new ones have a full 1TB of built-in space, so you can install a few extra games depending on how big they are.</p><h2 id="ps5-vs-ps5-slim-disc-drive">PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: disc drive</h2><p>Just like at the PS5's launch in late 2020, there are two PS5 Slim models. One of them has a built-in disc drive and the other one is digital-only.</p><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">
    <div class="flex justify-center">
                    <img class="w-full" src="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-4.fill.size_2000x1334.v1697141760.jpg" alt="PS5 Slim laying on its side" width="2000" height="1334" loading="lazy" srcset="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-4.fill.size_800x534.v1697141760.jpg 800w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-4.fill.size_1400x934.v1697141760.jpg 1400w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05Uv3oG3o5kh6djZHmwyhOT/images-4.fill.size_2000x1334.v1697141760.jpg 2000w" sizes="(max-width: 1408px) 100vw, 1408px">


            </div>
            <div class="mt-2 subtitle-2 font-sans ">
            <span class="normal-case text-gray-1000"></span>
            <span class="text-gray-600 credit">Credit: Sony</span>
        </div>
    </div>
<p>Well, sort of, anyway. There's an optional detachable disc drive you can buy for $79.99. It's a little goofy looking, but it should do exactly what you think it does. For physical media collectors, the disc drive is a must-buy.</p><p>It's worth noting, however, that the PS5 Slim, unlike the OG PS5, does <em>not </em>come with a vertical stand in the box. However, seasoned gamers will tell you that you should <a href="https://www.resetera.com/threads/you-might-be-killing-your-playstation-5-by-using-it-vertically-according-to-one-internet-article-unproven-rumor.672190/" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body" title="(opens in a new window)">keep your PS5 to be stationed horizontally anyway</a>.</p>

Expert advice on how Sony's PS5 Slim model is different from the original.  By  Alex Perry Alex Perry Tech Reporter Alex Perry is a tech reporter at Mashable who primarily covers video games and consumer tech. Alex has spent most of the last decade reviewing games, smartphones, headphones, and laptops, and he doesn’t plan on stopping anytime soon. He is also a Pisces, a cat lover, and a Kansas City sports fan. Alex can be found on Bluesky at yelix.bsky.social . If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission. How does PS5 Slim differ from the original PS5? Credit: Bob Al-Greene / Mashable Table of Contents Table of Contents Table of Contents PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: price PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: size PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: performance and storage PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: disc drive I've been using PlayStation consoles for almost 30 years. So in this PS5 vs. PS5 Slim face off, I'll be helping you decide which console is best for you. With the recent launch of the upgraded PS5 Pro console , now might be the perfect opportunity to snag a slightly older — yet still incredibly powerful — PS5. With potential sweet deals, or even permanent price drops on the horizon, it’s essential to know exactly what you’re getting (and not getting) with the PS5 and PS5 Slim. You May Also Like SEE ALSO: The price of Sony's PS5 Pro is 'brutal' and the internet hates it PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: price For context, the original, non-slim PS5 has two versions: a digital one (without a disc drive) and one with a disc drive. The same can be said for the PS5 Slim; it's got a digital version and a disc one. For whatever reason, Sony decided to not drop the prices of the new PS5 Slim models. The PS5 Slim with a disc drive is still $499, while the PS5 Slim without a disc drive is $449 — or a $50 increase over the original PS5 digital-only console . PS5 Slim (no disc drive) - $449 PS5 Slim (with disc drive) - $499 Original PS5 (no disc drive) - $399 Original PS5 (disc drive) - $499 PS5 Slim (no disc drive) $494.40 at Amazon   Shop Now at Amazon Shop Now at PlayStation Store Sony PlayStation 5 $704.99 at Walmart   Get Deal at Walmart Get Deal at Amazon Get Deal at Amazon With that in mind, yes, the digital-only PS5 Slim is a money-saver in comparison to the one with a disc drive, but not in comparison to the digital-only model that launched in 2020. The new price also means that buying a digital model before purchasing the additional disc drive would cost more than just snagging the version with a built-in drive. I don't really have a good explanation for that. Mashable Light Speed Want more out-of-this world tech, space and science stories? Sign up for Mashable's weekly Light Speed newsletter. Loading... My only advice is this: If you want a PS5 that only costs $399, you better get one now. This is an important note: Once the existing stock of both original models sells out, the new slim models will replace them on store shelves. PS5 vs. PS5 Slim: size Obviously, size is what many gamers are most concerned about here, so let's get right to it. Looking at Sony's stated dimensions, you can see that the new PS5 is indeed smaller than the original: Original PS5 (disc version) : 104mm (height) x 390mm (width) x 260mm (depth) PS5 Slim (disc version): 96mm (height) x 358mm (width) x 216mm (depth) Original PS5 (digital version) : 92mm x 390mm x 260mm PS5 Slim (digital version) : 80mm x 358mm x 216mm Credit: Sony In other words, per Sony's announcement blog post , that's about a 30 percent reduction in total volume. That's definitely an improvement, but there's some important context missing in just those raw numbers. The Verge ran a digital size comparison and discovered that both new models are still substantially larger than the Xbox Series X. In other words, this "slim" console is still pretty dang big. For a visual comparison, check out this awesome PS5 Slim vs. Regular Reddit post. This isn't a PS4 vs. PS4 Pro situation. Games will run exactly the same across the spectrum of PS5 consoles. The tech giant announced the Apple Watch Series 12 during its Sept. 9 "Surprise and Shine" iPhone event, along with the new Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the first-ever foldable iPhone Duo. In a press release, Apple’s Vice President of Worldwide iPhone Product Marketing Kaiann Drance called the Series 12 "the most advanced health and fitness companion we’ve ever created." You might not know that at a glance because it looks the same as last year's Series 11. To find out what's actually new about the Series 12, you have to peek inside its case.

Here's a full breakdown of the main differences between the Apple Watch Series 12 and Series 11, including one notable upgrade that Apple didn't mention in its keynote presentation. (Spoiler: it has something to do with memory.)Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Pricing
    
                    


            
            
            The Series 12 has the same $399 base price as the Series 11 (pictured here).
            Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable
        
    
Now available for preorder, the Series 12 starts at $399 with a 42mm aluminum case — the same price as the base Series 11. However, the 46mm Series 12 starts at $449, which is a $20 bump from the previous generation. There's now a $50 difference separating the two sizes, no matter the case material.The 42mm and 46mm titanium variants of the Series 12 start at $699 and $749, respectively, just like their Series 11 counterparts. 
        SEE ALSO:
        
            How to preorder the new Apple Watches, including the Series 12 and Ultra 4
            
        
    
The Series 12 comes in a third "new" ceramic variant that starts at $899 for the 42mm size and $949 for the 46mm model. (The Series 11 wasn't available with a ceramic case, but the much older Series 2, 3, and 5 all came in that scratch-resistant material.)
        SEE ALSO:
        
            How to preorder the new Apple Watches, including the Series 12 and Ultra 4
            
        
    
Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: DesignThe Series 12 has the same external design as the Series 11 — and the Series 10, for that matter. Apple hasn't changed the look of its flagship wearable since that 2024 release, when it got a thinner, lighter case and a more rounded display. (The rumor mill says a proper redesign is coming next year.) Additionally, it's still IP6X dust-resistant and water-resistant for up to 50 meters.That said, the aluminum Series 12 variants got one small tweak. Their Ceramic Shield 2 glass is more durable than the Ion-X glass on their Series 11 counterparts. Apple said it's "60 percent tougher," to be exact.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Display
    
                    


            
            
            This is a picture of the Apple Watch Series 11, but it's also kind of a picture of the Series 12. They're virtually identical.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
Both Apple Watches have the same always-on, wide-angle OLED display with up to 2,000 nits of brightness. That's very, very bright.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Colors
    
                    


            
            
            The Apple Watch Series 12 comes in eight different case material/color combinations.
            Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable
        
    
The Series 12's case comes in the following case colors:Aluminum: Dark bronze, light gold, black, space grayTitanium: Radiant gold and naturalCeramic: Pearl white and night blueThe Series 11's case came in fewer colorways:Aluminum: Rose gold, silver, space gray, and jet blackTitanium: Natural, gold, and slateApple introduced a bunch of new band colors and materials for the Series 12 that would also fit the Series 11, if you want to freshen up one you already own. You can buy them separately starting at $49.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Specs
    
                    


            
            
            The Series 12's S11 chip has more muscle than the Series 11's S10 chip.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
The Series 11 ran on the S10 chip, while the Series 12 is powered by the newer S11 chip — "Apple’s most powerful wearable chip," the company said. It enables several new features that I'll elaborate on shortly.Notably, MacRumors reports that the Series 12 has twice as much memory as the Series 11 (4GB versus 2GB). Apple didn't mention that during its iPhone event this week, but the company's Xcode 27 developer tool reportedly shows evidence of it, the tech site said. If true, the Series 12's mostly unchanged prices are quite the feat: RAM costs have skyrocketed in the past year. (That's the reason why Apple raised its MacBook and iPad prices this summer, and probably its logic behind recent iPhone price hikes, too.)The Series 12 maintains the same storage capacity as the Series 11: 64GB.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Cellular connectivityLike the Series 11, the Series 12 is available with 5G cellular connectivity. It's still a $100 upgrade on the aluminum variants and a standard feature on the titanium (and now ceramic) versions.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Battery lifeThe Series 12 and 11 are both rated for up to 24 hours of battery life per charge, which you can extend to 38 hours by putting them in Low Power Mode. However, the Series 12's charging speed got a boost. A quick 15-minute power-up provides up to 12 hours of normal usage, up from eight hours in the Series 11.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Sensors
    
                    


            
            
            The Series 12's Health Sensing System is only available on one other Apple Watch, that being the new Ultra 4.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
Here's where things start to get more interesting. The Series 12 has a new Health Sensing System with upgraded optical and electrical sensors that measure the user's heart rate continuously and more accurately. You can see the glowing green lights of the optical sensor on the underside of its case.Apple said this system measures heart rate every five seconds all day long. It also captures heart rate variability (HRV) data, a stress and recovery metric, up to 24 times more often.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Features
    
                    


            
            
            Should you skip leg day or power through? Your Series 12 can tell you.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
The Series 12 and 11 both run on watchOS and share the same core health, wellness, and safety features, including Sleep Score, Hypertension and Sleep Apnea Notifications, Cycle Tracking, Fall and Crash Detection, Emergency SOS, and the AI-powered Workout Buddy. They'll also both support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which arrives with the release of watchOS 27 on Sept. 14. However, the Series 12 brings a few exclusive new features to the table courtesy of its upgraded chip and sensors:Readiness, a feature that tells the user how prepared they are (or not) for future fitness activities based on their recent workouts, vitals, and sleep patternsAudio Intelligence tools that use its built-in microphone, including Sound Recognition alerts, Live Rewind conversation transcriptions, and Siri Recap conversation summariesMore accurate step tracking powered by a revamped pedometer model, including a Steps complication (finally!)Do these small hardware tweaks and new features make the Series 12 worth the upgrade? Stay tuned for Mashable's full review to find out — we just got our hands on a review unit for testing. <h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-design">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Design</h2><p>The Series 12 has the same external design as the Series 11 — and the <a href="https://mashable.com/review/apple-watch-series-10" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">Series 10</a>, for that matter. Apple hasn't changed the look of its flagship wearable since that 2024 release, when it got a thinner, lighter case and a more rounded display. (The rumor mill says a <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-series-12-rumors-upgrades" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">proper redesign</a> is coming next year.) Their Ceramic Shield 2 glass is more durable than the Ion-X glass on their Series 11 counterparts. <p>The Series 12's case comes in the following case colors:</p><ul><li><p>Aluminum: Dark bronze, light gold, black, space gray</p></li><li><p>Titanium: Radiant gold and natural</p></li><li><p>Ceramic: Pearl white and night blue</p></li></ul><p>The Series 11's case came in fewer colorways:</p><ul><li><p>Aluminum: Rose gold, silver, space gray, and jet black</p></li><li><p>Titanium: Natural, gold, and slate</p></li></ul><p>Apple introduced a bunch of new band colors and materials for the Series 12 that would also fit the Series 11, if you want to freshen up one you already own. You can buy them separately <a href="https://zdcs.link/zJ76kg?pageview_type=Standard&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=starting%20at%20%2449&object_type=article&object_uuid=01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq&short_url=zJ76kg&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Farticle-route-prefix%2Ftech%2Fapple-watch-series-12-vs-11-price-specs" rel="sponsored"  target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body" title="(opens in a new window)">starting at $49</a>.</p><h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-specs">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Specs</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">
    <div class="flex justify-center">
                    <img class="w-full" src="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-5.fill.size_2000x1334.v1789075296.jpg" alt="a woman working out while wearing the apple watch series 12" width="2000" height="1334" loading="lazy" srcset="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-5.fill.size_800x533.v1789075296.jpg 800w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-5.fill.size_1400x934.v1789075296.jpg 1400w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-5.fill.size_2000x1334.v1789075296.jpg 2000w" sizes="(max-width: 1408px) 100vw, 1408px">

<p>The Series 11 ran on the S10 chip, while the Series 12 is powered by the newer S11 chip — "Apple’s most powerful wearable chip," the company said. It enables several new features that I'll elaborate on shortly.</p><p>Notably, <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/10/apple-watch-series-12-ultra-4-increased-ram/" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body" title="(opens in a new window)">MacRumors</a> reports that the Series 12 has twice as much memory as the Series 11 (4GB versus 2GB). Apple didn't mention that during its iPhone event this week, but the company's Xcode 27 developer tool reportedly shows evidence of it, the tech site said. If true, the Series 12's mostly unchanged prices are quite the feat: <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/ramageddon-every-tech-price-increase-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">RAM costs have skyrocketed</a> in the past year. (That's the reason why Apple raised its <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-price-increases-full-list" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">MacBook and iPad prices</a> this summer, and probably its logic behind recent <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/iphone-18-pro-price-hike-confirmed" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">iPhone</a> <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/iphone-price-increase-apple-16-17-air" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">price hikes</a>, too.)</p><p>The Series 12 maintains the same storage capacity as the Series 11: 64GB.</p><div class="related-stories" data-ga-impression data-ga-module="related_stories" data-ga-element="related_stories_link" data-ga-item="title">

<h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-cellular-connectivity">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Cellular connectivity</h2><p>Like the Series 11, the Series 12 is available with 5G cellular connectivity. It's still a $100 upgrade on the aluminum variants and a standard feature on the titanium (and now ceramic) versions.</p><h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-battery-life">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Battery life</h2><p>The Series 12 and 11 are both rated for up to 24 hours of battery life per charge, which you can extend to 38 hours by putting them in Low Power Mode. However, the Series 12's charging speed got a boost. A quick 15-minute power-up provides up to 12 hours of normal usage, up from eight hours in the Series 11.</p><h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-sensors">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Sensors</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">
    <div class="flex justify-center">
                    <img class="w-full" src="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-1.fill.size_2000x1124.v1789074654.jpg" alt="the front and back of the Apple Watch Series 12" width="2000" height="1124" loading="lazy" srcset="https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-1.fill.size_800x450.v1789074654.jpg 800w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-1.fill.size_1400x787.v1789074654.jpg 1400w, https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01x0H7AdKnXe9mTOVdAHzgq/images-1.fill.size_2000x1124.v1789074654.jpg 2000w" sizes="(max-width: 1408px) 100vw, 1408px">

    </div>
<p>Here's where things start to get more interesting. The Series 12 has a new Health Sensing System with upgraded optical and electrical sensors that measure the user's heart rate continuously and more accurately. You can see the glowing green lights of the optical sensor on the underside of its case.</p><p>Apple said this system measures heart rate every five seconds all day long. It also captures heart rate variability (HRV) data, a stress and recovery metric, up to 24 times more often.</p><h2 id="apple-watch-series-12-vs-series-11-features">Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Features</h2><div class="eloquent-imagery-image">
    <div class="flex justify-center">

            </div>
            <div class="mt-2 subtitle-2 font-sans ">
            <span class="normal-case text-gray-1000">Should you skip leg day or power through? Your Series 12 can tell you.</span>
            <span class="text-gray-600 credit">Credit: Apple</span>
        </div>
    </div>
<p>The Series 12 and 11 both run on <a href="https://mashable.com/article/apple-watch-watchos-26-wwdc-2025" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">watchOS</a> and share the same core health, wellness, and safety features, including Sleep Score, Hypertension and Sleep Apnea Notifications, Cycle Tracking, Fall and Crash Detection, Emergency SOS, and the AI-powered Workout Buddy. They'll also both support <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-intelligence-updates-wwdc-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">Apple Intelligence</a> and <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/siri-ai-beta-apple-intelligence-updates-iphone-event-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">Siri AI</a>, which arrives with the release of <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/watchos-27-wwdc-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">watchOS 27</a> on Sept. 14. </p><p>However, the Series 12 brings a few exclusive new features to the table courtesy of its upgraded chip and sensors:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Readiness</strong>, a feature that tells the user how prepared they are (or not) for future fitness activities based on their recent workouts, vitals, and sleep patterns</p></li><li><p><strong>Audio Intelligence</strong> tools that use its built-in microphone, including Sound Recognition alerts, Live Rewind conversation transcriptions, and <a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-siri-ai-conversation-recap-iphone-event-2026" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">Siri Recap</a> conversation summaries</p></li><li><p><strong>More accurate step tracking</strong> powered by a revamped pedometer model, including a Steps complication (<a href="https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-step-count-widget-hacks" target="_blank" data-ga-click="1" data-ga-label="$text" data-ga-item="text-link" data-ga-module="content_body">finally!</a>)</p></li></ul><p>Do these small hardware tweaks and new features make the Series 12 worth the upgrade? In a press release , Apple’s Vice President of Worldwide iPhone Product Marketing Kaiann Drance called the Series 12 "the most advanced health and fitness companion we’ve ever created." You might not know that at a glance because it looks the same as last year's Series 11. To find out what's actually new about the Series 12, you have to peek inside its case. Credit: Stan Schroeder / Mashable Now available for preorder , the Series 12 starts at $399 with a 42mm aluminum case — the same price as the base Series 11. However, the 46mm Series 12 starts at $449, which is a $20 bump from the previous generation. There's now a $50 difference separating the two sizes, no matter the case material. The 42mm and 46mm titanium variants of the Series 12 start at $699 and $749, respectively, just like their Series 11 counterparts. SEE ALSO: How to preorder the new Apple Watches, including the Series 12 and Ultra 4 The Series 12 comes in a third "new" ceramic variant that starts at $899 for the 42mm size and $949 for the 46mm model. (The Series 11 wasn't available with a ceramic case, but the much older Series 2, 3, and 5 all came in that scratch-resistant material.) You can buy them separately starting at $49 . Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Specs The Series 12's S11 chip has more muscle than the Series 11's S10 chip. Credit: Apple The Series 11 ran on the S10 chip, while the Series 12 is powered by the newer S11 chip — "Apple’s most powerful wearable chip," the company said. It enables several new features that I'll elaborate on shortly. Notably, MacRumors reports that the Series 12 has twice as much memory as the Series 11 (4GB versus 2GB). Apple didn't mention that during its iPhone event this week, but the company's Xcode 27 developer tool reportedly shows evidence of it, the tech site said. If true, the Series 12's mostly unchanged prices are quite the feat: RAM costs have skyrocketed in the past year. (That's the reason why Apple raised its MacBook and iPad prices this summer, and probably its logic behind recent iPhone price hikes , too.) The Series 12 maintains the same storage capacity as the Series 11: 64GB. Related Stories Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 first look: AI and major health upgrades! Apple's Siri Recap will remember your conversations for you 5 Apple product launches we still expect to see in 2026 Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Cellular connectivity Like the Series 11, the Series 12 is available with 5G cellular connectivity. It's still a $100 upgrade on the aluminum variants and a standard feature on the titanium (and now ceramic) versions. Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Battery life The Series 12 and 11 are both rated for up to 24 hours of battery life per charge, which you can extend to 38 hours by putting them in Low Power Mode. However, the Series 12's charging speed got a boost. A quick 15-minute power-up provides up to 12 hours of normal usage, up from eight hours in the Series 11. Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Sensors The Series 12's Health Sensing System is only available on one other Apple Watch, that being the new Ultra 4. Credit: Apple Here's where things start to get more interesting. The Series 12 has a new Health Sensing System with upgraded optical and electrical sensors that measure the user's heart rate continuously and more accurately. You can see the glowing green lights of the optical sensor on the underside of its case. Apple said this system measures heart rate every five seconds all day long. It also captures heart rate variability (HRV) data, a stress and recovery metric, up to 24 times more often. Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Features Should you skip leg day or power through? Your Series 12 can tell you. They'll also both support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI , which arrives with the release of watchOS 27 on Sept. 14. However, the Series 12 brings a few exclusive new features to the table courtesy of its upgraded chip and sensors: Readiness , a feature that tells the user how prepared they are (or not) for future fitness activities based on their recent workouts, vitals, and sleep patterns Audio Intelligence tools that use its built-in microphone, including Sound Recognition alerts, Live Rewind conversation transcriptions, and Siri Recap conversation summaries More accurate step tracking powered by a revamped pedometer model, including a Steps complication ( finally! ) Do these small hardware tweaks and new features make the Series 12 worth the upgrade? It's still a $100 upgrade on the aluminum variants and a standard feature on the titanium (and now ceramic) versions.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Battery lifeThe Series 12 and 11 are both rated for up to 24 hours of battery life per charge, which you can extend to 38 hours by putting them in Low Power Mode. However, the Series 12's charging speed got a boost. A quick 15-minute power-up provides up to 12 hours of normal usage, up from eight hours in the Series 11.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Sensors
    
                    


            
            
            The Series 12's Health Sensing System is only available on one other Apple Watch, that being the new Ultra 4.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
Here's where things start to get more interesting. The Series 12 has a new Health Sensing System with upgraded optical and electrical sensors that measure the user's heart rate continuously and more accurately. You can see the glowing green lights of the optical sensor on the underside of its case.Apple said this system measures heart rate every five seconds all day long. It also captures heart rate variability (HRV) data, a stress and recovery metric, up to 24 times more often.Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Series 11: Features
    
                    


            
            
            Should you skip leg day or power through? Your Series 12 can tell you.
            Credit: Apple
        
    
The Series 12 and 11 both run on watchOS and share the same core health, wellness, and safety features, including Sleep Score, Hypertension and Sleep Apnea Notifications, Cycle Tracking, Fall and Crash Detection, Emergency SOS, and the AI-powered Workout Buddy. They'll also both support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which arrives with the release of watchOS 27 on Sept. 14. However, the Series 12 brings a few exclusive new features to the table courtesy of its upgraded chip and sensors:Readiness, a feature that tells the user how prepared they are (or not) for future fitness activities based on their recent workouts, vitals, and sleep patternsAudio Intelligence tools that use its built-in microphone, including Sound Recognition alerts, Live Rewind conversation transcriptions, and Siri Recap conversation summariesMore accurate step tracking powered by a revamped pedometer model, including a Steps complication (finally!)Do these small hardware tweaks and new features make the Series 12 worth the upgrade? Stay tuned for Mashable's full review to find out — we just got our hands on a review unit for testing.
